text:
marco: hi team, i'm marco — new runtime dev. i'm on an M2 laptop and want to iterate on the runtime source. what's the lowest friction path for build/test without an nvidia gpu? :wave:
linh: welcome! for day-to-day we do CPU builds locally and use the build fleet for GPU-only steps. you can also use our cpu Docker image for a reproducible env.
omar: avoid trying to install CUDA on mac. if you need nvcc you should SSH to the linux gpu hosts.
marco: ok. i tried the cpu docker image but cmake still errors trying to find CUDA headers. any env flags to skip that probe?
linh: yeah, export SKIP_CUDA_PROBE=1 before cmake, or pass -DENABLE_CUDA=OFF. both skip nvcc checks in our CMakeLists.
marco: SKIP_CUDA_PROBE worked, thanks. after switching to the remote host (i got SSH after filing a ticket) the build fails with `ptxas: error: Unsupported gpu architecture 'compute_61'` — host is A100.
omar: set TARGET_ARCH=sm_80 in your shell before building or edit tools/select-kernels.sh. some older PRs added legacy arch flags.
marco: TARGET_ARCH=sm_80 fixed that. two quick follow-ups: 1) is there a canonical docker image for GPU smoke runs? 2) any quick checklist for week one?
eva: yes — gpu image is redwood/dev-gpu:ci. once you have ssh cert you can run it on the host `docker run --rm -it -v $PWD:/work redwood/dev-gpu:ci /bin/bash`. checklist: clone + submodules, ./scripts/bootstrap --dev, build cpu w/ SKIP_CUDA_PROBE, run unit tests, request gpu access, run ./scripts/build --target=gpu on host, run tools/perf/run_smoke.sh and ping your mentor for pairing.
marco: perfect. re: ssh ticket — devops-bot, any ETA on approvals for new hires?
devops-bot: approvals typically take 1 business day after manager sign-off. include your team and manager in the ticket to speed it up.
marco: got it — will open ticket now and post the number. thanks all! :thumbsup:
